label: SELF-WORTH

cover.headline: Rebuilding confidence *after being cheated on*
cover.sub: 5 reminders for the days it stings.

points.heading: It wasn’t your fault
points.body: Someone else’s choice to cheat isn’t a measure of your worth.
points.panel: “His choice says nothing about my value.”

points.heading: Let yourself be angry
points.body: Anger is a normal, healthy response to betrayal.
points.panel: Write an unsent letter and say everything.

points.heading: Stop comparing yourself
points.body: Comparing yourself to the other person keeps the hurt alive.
points.panel: “This isn’t a contest, and I’m not competing.”

points.heading: Rebuild trust in yourself
points.body: Notice the moments your instincts were right.
points.panel: “When did my gut try to tell me something?”

points.heading: Take trust slowly next time
points.body: It’s okay to let trust build gradually.
points.panel: “I can be open and still go slowly.”

close.save: Save this for the hard days.

caption:
Being cheated on can shake your confidence in ways that last long after the relationship ends.

It wasn’t your fault, and it doesn’t define your worth. These five reminders help you rebuild trust in yourself first, so you can trust others again, slowly and wisely, when you’re ready.

Save this for the hard days, and follow @roundabloom for more gentle steps.
